content: {"summary":"On 10 Mar 2026 the /search endpoint returned 429 EDGE‑RL01 responses from all three edge pods while search‑api remained calm. The edge limiter allowed only 300 requests per second total (≈40 refused per pod) and the campaign traffic rose to ~420 rps, exceeding that limit. The limit was originally set when the route was created and never updated despite traffic growth, and the limiter settings are stored in a ConfigMap read only at Envoy startup, so changing the limit required a rolling restart of the edge pods.","likely_cause":"Edge rate‑limit exceeded because the static 300 rps limit was too low for the increased March 2026 campaign traffic.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"The edge rate‑limit allowed 300 requests per second total across the three edge pods.","evidence_ids":["RB-030#1"],"quote":"With 300 allowed, about 120 a second were refused, around 29%, or roughly 40 a second on each pod."},{"text":"The limit was set when the route was first created and had not been updated despite growing search traffic.","evidence_ids":["RB-030#1"],"quote":"The limit went in when the route was first set up, as a guard against crawlers."},{"text":"Limiter settings live in the ConfigMap edge‑gateway‑envoy and are read only at Envoy startup, so a change required a rolling restart of edge pods.","evidence_ids":["RB-030#3"],"quote":"The limiter's settings live in the ConfigMap `edge-gateway-envoy`, and Envoy reads them only at startup."}],"next_checks":["Inspect the current edge‑gateway‑envoy ConfigMap for the /search rate‑limit value","Confirm whether the limit was increased after the incident","Verify that a rolling restart applied any new limit configuration","Monitor edge pod request rates during future campaign sends"]}
